base_member_text: Serial CARTESIAN INITIAL_RECTANGULAR (L231-234) lacks the out-of-window clipping applied in the parallel branch (L220-227); Il<1 or Ir>M would produce an invalid array section.
audit_member_text: The parallel INITIAL_RECTANGULAR branch clips Il/Ir/Jl/Jr to array limits and handles no-overlap, while the serial branch writes Eta(Il:Ir,Jl:Jr) without any clipping. Rectangles partly or wholly outside the serial grid can create invalid sections or runtime bounds errors.

base_member_text: INITIAL_N_WAVE: dummy gamma_s (L439, L447) is never used; x2 appears only in the commented general n-wave formula (L490); local tlag (L71 in SOLITARY_WAVE_LEFT_BOUNDARY) likewise assigned but unused.
audit_member_text: INITIAL_N_WAVE accepts gamma_s and x2 but never uses either in active code; the x2-dependent general N-wave expression is commented and gamma is recomputed locally. The public interface therefore advertises controls that do not affect output.

base_member_text: INITIAL_WAVE (L95-160) is effectively dead code: goto 200 (L123), goto 100 (L135) and goto 213 (L150) skip the box (L124-131), dam-break (L136-141) and alongshore-crest (L151-157) blocks, and the gaussian is commented (L144-145), so Eta is never modified; sigma/x_c/y_c/a (L116-119) and XX/YY (L104-114) are computed but unused.
audit_member_text: INITIAL_WAVE is effectively a no-op for Eta: unconditional `goto 200` skips the box assignment, unconditional `goto 100` skips the dam-break assignment, the Gaussian assignment is commented, and `goto 213` skips the alongshore crest. XX/YY and scalar parameters are computed but no active initial field is written.

base_member_text: tmp1/tmp2 used in INITIAL_WAVE (L125-127) and tmp1 in INITIAL_N_WAVE (L473-486) are not locally declared despite IMPLICIT NONE -- must be module variables from USE GLOBAL/PARAM; same for loop indices I,J in the INTENT-based subroutines (e.g. L283-284, L466-467).

alpha=-0.39 hardcoded (L534) replaces the commented formula alpha=0.5_SP*Beta*Beta+Beta (L531); comments L532-533 record that the resulting wave shape does not match the equation ('alpha = -0.10 seems OK'); the Beta dummy (L525) is consequently unused.
SUB_SLTRY: zr (L632) is computed but is neither an OUT argument nor used; r1 (L617) and C_ph (L618) receive the identical value rx*cph; local cph shadows the caller's Cph actual argument bound to r1.
INITIAL_GAUSIAN header comment (L251) says input keyword 'INI_REC' although the routine is the gaussian hump (dipole header L340 correctly says 'INI_DIP').
Newton loop failure paths only stop without message: explanatory write commented at L611 (SUB_SLTRY) and L456 (INITIAL_N_WAVE depth guard).

audit_member_text: INITIAL_SOLITARY_WAVE accepts Beta and even shows the intended alpha formula in a comment, but unconditionally assigns alpha=-0.39 before calling SUB_SLTRY. Thus Beta does not affect the generated solution and all caller-selected beta values collapse to one profile.

Gaussian and dipole formulas divide by WID and WID**2 without a positive-width check. SOLITARY_WAVE_LEFT_BOUNDARY and SUB_SLTRY similarly divide by h00/h1 and amplitude ratios without validating their domains.

SUB_SLTRY performs x=x-fx/fpx before checking iteration count and never guards fpx=0. Subsequent SQRT expressions require x and (alp2-alp*x) domains that are also unchecked, so the advertised STOP path does not protect singular Newton steps or invalid roots.

For non-Cartesian variable spacing, INITIAL_WAVE, INITIAL_N_WAVE and INITIAL_SOLITARY_WAVE estimate position by multiplying a local DX(I,J) by an index rather than accumulating cell widths. Correctness therefore depends on DX being uniform despite its array-valued interface.
The file banner says sample.F while the actual path is samples.F; this is a provenance-name mismatch.
